layout_dets.text: Medical image segmentation is a critical component in clinical practice, facil-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: itating accurate diagnosis, treatment planning, and disease monitoring.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: However, existing methods, often tailored to specific modalities or disease

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: types, lack generalizability across the diverse spectrum of medical image

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: segmentation tasks. Here we present MedSAM, a foundation model designed

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: for bridging this gap by enabling universal medical image segmentation. The

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: model is developed on a large-scale medical image dataset with 1,570,263

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: image-mask pairs, covering 10 imaging modalities and over 30 cancer types.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We conduct a comprehensive evaluation on 86 internal validation tasks and 60

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: external validation tasks, demonstrating better accuracy and robustness than

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: modality-wise specialist models. By delivering accurate and efficient seg-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mentation across a wide spectrum of tasks, MedSAM holds significant

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: potential to expedite the evolution of diagnostic tools and the personalization

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of treatment plans.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Segmentation is a fundamental task in medical imaging analysis, which

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: involves identifying and delineating regions of interest (ROI) in various

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: medical images, such as organs, lesions, and tissues¹. Accurate seg-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mentation is essential for many clinical applications, including disease

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: diagnosis, treatment planning, and monitoring of disease

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: progression²³. Manual segmentation has long been the gold standard

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: for delineating anatomical structures and pathological regions, but

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: this process is time-consuming, labor-intensive, and often requires a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: high degree of expertise. Semi- or fully automatic segmentation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: methods can significantly reduce the time and labor required, increase

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: consistency, and enable the analysis of large-scale datasets⁴.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Deep learning-based models have shown great promise in medical

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: image segmentation due to their ability to learn intricate image fea-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tures and deliver accurate segmentation results across a diverse range

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of tasks, from segmenting specific anatomical structures to identifying

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pathological regions⁵. However, a significant limitation of many cur-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: rent medical image segmentation models is their task-specific nature.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: These models are typically designed and trained for a specific seg-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mentation task, and their performance can degrade significantly when

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: applied to new tasks or different types of imaging data6. This lack of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: generality poses a substantial obstacle to the wider application of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: these models in clinical practice. In contrast, recent advances in the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: field of natural image segmentation have witnessed the emergence of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: segmentation foundation models, such as segment anything model

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (SAM)7 and Segment Everything Everywhere with Multi-modal

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: prompts all at once8, showcasing remarkable versatility and perfor-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mance across various segmentation tasks.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: There is a growing demand for universal models in medical image

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: segmentation: models that can be trained once and then applied to a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: wide range of segmentation tasks. Such models would not only exhibit

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: heightened versatility in terms of model capacity but also potentially

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: lead to more consistent results across different tasks. However, the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: applicability of the segmentation foundation models (e.g., SAM) to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: medical image segmentation remains limited due to the significant

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: differences between natural images and medical images. Essentially,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: SAM is a promptable segmentation method that requires points or

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: bounding boxes to specify the segmentation targets. This resembles

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: conventional interactive segmentation methods4,9-11but SAM has bet-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ter generalization ability, while existing deep learning-based inter-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: active segmentation methods focus mainly on limited tasks and image

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: modalities.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Many studies have applied the out-of-the-box SAM models to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: typical medical image segmentation tasks12-17and other challenging

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: scenarios18-21. For example, the concurrent studies22,23conducted a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion performance of SAM on medical images. MedSAM accomplishes

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: this by fine-tuning SAM on an unprecedented dataset with more than

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We thoroughly evaluate MedSAM through comprehensive

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: experiments on 86 internal validation tasks and 60 external validation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tasks, spanning a variety of anatomical structures, pathological con-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ditions, and medical imaging modalities. Experimental results

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: demonstrate that MedSAM consistently outperforms the state-of-the-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: art (SOTA) segmentation foundation model7, while achieving perfor-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mance on par with, or even surpassing specialist models1,24that were

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: trained on the images from the same modality. These results highlight

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the potential of MedSAM as a new paradigm for versatile medical

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: image segmentation.

layout_dets.text: Results

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: MedSAM: a foundation model for promptable medical image

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: segmentation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: MedSAM aims to fulfill the role of a foundation model for universal

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: medical image segmentation. A crucial aspect of constructing such a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: model is the capacity to accommodate a wide range of variations in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: imaging conditions, anatomical structures, and pathological condi-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tions. To address this challenge, we curated a diverse and large-scale

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: medical image segmentation dataset with 1,570,263 medical image-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mask pairs, covering 10 imaging modalities, over 30 cancer types, and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a multitude of imaging protocols (Fig. 1 and Supplementary

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Tables 1-4). This large-scale dataset allows MedSAM to learn a rich

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: representation of medical images, capturing a broad spectrum of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: anatomies and lesions across different modalities. Figure 2a provides

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: an overview of the distribution of images across different medical

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: imaging modalities in the dataset, ranked by their total numbers. It is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: evident that computed tomography (CT), magnetic resonance ima-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ging (MRI), and endoscopy are the dominant modalities, reflecting

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: their ubiquity in clinical practice. CT and MRI images provide detailed

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cross-sectional views of 3D body structures, making them indis-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pensable for non-invasive diagnostic imaging. Endoscopy, albeit more

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: invasive, enables direct visual inspection of organ interiors, proving

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: invaluable for diagnosing gastrointestinal and urological conditions.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Despite the prevalence of these modalities, others such as ultrasound,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pathology, fundus, dermoscopy, mammography, and optical coher-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ence tomography (OCT) also hold significant roles in clinical practice.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The diversity of these modalities and their corresponding segmenta-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion targets underscores the necessity for universal and effective

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: segmentation models capable of handling the unique characteristics

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: associated with each modality.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Another critical consideration is the selection of the appropriate

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: segmentation prompt and network architecture. While the concept of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: fully automatic segmentation foundation models is enticing, it is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: fraught with challenges that make it impractical. One of the primary

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: challenges is the variability inherent in segmentation tasks. For

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: example, given a liver cancer CT image, the segmentation task can vary

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: depending on the specific clinical scenario. One clinician might be

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: interested in segmenting the liver tumor, while another might need to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: segment the entire liver and surrounding organs. Additionally, the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: variability in imaging modalities presents another challenge. Mod-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: alities such as CT and MR generate 3D images, whereas others like

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: X-ray and ultrasound yield 2D images. These variabilities in task defi-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: nition and imaging modalities complicate the design of a fully auto-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: matic model capable of accurately anticipating and addressing the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: diverse requirements of different users.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Considering these challenges, we argue that a more practical

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: approach is to develop a promptable 2D segmentation model. The

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: model can be easily adapted to specific tasks based on user-provided

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: prompts, offering enhanced flexibility and adaptability. It is also able

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to handle both 2D and 3D images by processing 3D images as a series

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of 2D slices. Typical user prompts include points and bounding boxes

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and we show some segmentation examples with the different prompts

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in Supplementary Fig. 1. It can be found that bounding boxes provide a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: more unambiguous spatial context for the region of interest, enabling

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the algorithm to more precisely discern the target area. This stands in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: contrast to point-based prompts, which can introduce ambiguity,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: particularly when proximate structures resemble each other. More-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: over, drawing a bounding box is efficient, especially in scenarios

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: involving multi-object segmentation. We follow the network archi-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tecture in SAM7, including an image encoder, a prompt encoder, and a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mask decoder (Fig. 2b). The image encoder²⁵maps the input image

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: into a high-dimensional image embedding space. The prompt encoder

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: transforms the user-drawn bounding boxes into feature representa-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tions via positional encoding26. Finally, the mask decoder fuses the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: image embedding and prompt features using cross-attention²7

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (Methods).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Quantitative and qualitative analysis

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We evaluated MedSAM through both internal validation and external

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: validation. Specifically, we compared it to the SOTA segmentation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: foundation model SAMas well as modality-wise specialist U-Net and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: DeepLabV3+²4 models. Each specialized model was trained on images

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: from the corresponding modality, resulting in 10 dedicated specialist

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: models for each method. During inference, these specialist models

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: were used to segment the images from corresponding modalities,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: while SAM and MedSAM were employed for segmenting images across

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: all modalities (Methods). The internal validation contained 86 seg-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mentation tasks (Supplementary Tables 5-8 and Fig. 2), and Fig. 3a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: shows the median dice similarity coefficient (DSC) score of these tasks

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: for the four methods. Overall, SAM obtained the lowest performance

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: on most segmentation tasks although it performed promisingly on

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: some RGB image segmentation tasks, such as polyp (DSC: 91.3%,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: interquartile range (IQR): 81.2-95.1%) segmentation in endoscopy

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: images. This could be attributed to SAM's training on a variety of RGB

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: images, and the fact that many targets in these images are relatively

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: straightforward to segment due to their distinct appearances. The

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: other three models outperformed SAM by a large margin and MedSAM

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: has a narrower distribution of DSC scores of the 86 interval validation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tasks than the two groups of specialist models, reflecting the robust-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ness of MedSAM across different tasks. We further connected the DSC

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: scores corresponding to the same task of the four models with the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: podium plot Fig. 3b, which is complementary to the box plot. In the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: upper part, each colored dot denotes the median DSC achieved with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the respective method on one task. Dots corresponding to identical

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: test cases are connected by a line. In the lower part, the frequency of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: achieved ranks for each method is presented with bar charts. It can be

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: found that MedSAM ranked in first place on most tasks, surpassing the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: performance of the U-Net and DeepLabV3+ specialist models that have

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a high frequency of ranks with second and third places, respectively, In

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: contrast, SAM ranked last place in almost all tasks. Figure 3c (and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Supplementary Fig. 9) visualizes some randomly selected segmenta-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion examples where MedSAM obtained a median DSC score, including

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: liver tumor in CT images, brain tumor in MR images, breast tumor in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ultrasound images, and polyp in endoscopy images. SAM struggles

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: with targets of weak boundaries, which is prone to under or over-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: segmentation errors. In contrast, MedSAM can accurately segment a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: wide range of targets across various imaging conditions, which

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: achieves comparable of even better than the specialist U-Net and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: DeepLabV3+ models.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The external validation included 60 segmentation tasks, all of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: which either were from new datasets or involved unseen segmen-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tation targets (Supplementary Tables 9-11 and Figs. 10-12). Fig-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ure 4a, b show the task-wise median DSC score distribution and their

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: correspondence of the 60 tasks, respectively. Although SAM con-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tinued exhibiting lower performance on most CT and MR segmen-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tation tasks, the specialist models no longer consistently

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: outperformed SAM (e.g., right kidney segmentation in MR T1-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: weighted images: 90.1%, 85.3%, 86.4% for SAM, U-Net, and Dee-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pLabV3+, respectively). This indicates the limited generalization

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ability of such specialist models on unseen targets. In contrast,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: MedSAM consistently delivers superior performance. For example,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: MedSAM obtained median DSC scores of 87.8% (IQR: 85.0-91.4%) on

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the nasopharynx cancer segmentation task, demonstrating 52.3%,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 15.5%, and 22.7 improvements over SAM, the specialist U-Net, and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: DeepLabV3+, respectively. Significantly, MedSAM also achieved

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: better performance in some unseen modalities (e.g., abdomen T1

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Inphase and Outphase), surpassing SAM and the specialist models

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: with improvements by up to 10%. Figure 4c presents four randomly

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: selected segmentation examples for qualitative evaluation, reveal-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ing that while all the methods have the ability to handle simple

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: segmentation targets, MedSAM performs better at segmenting

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: challenging targets with indistinguishable boundaries, such as cer-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: vical cancer in MR images (more examples are presented in Sup-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: plementary Fig. 13). Furthermore, we evaluated MedSAM on the

layout_dets.text: multiple myeloma plasma cell dataset, which represents a distinct

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: modality and task in contrast to all previously leveraged validation

layout_dets.text: tasks. Although this task had never been seen during training,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Furthermore, we conducted a human annotation study to assess the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: time cost of two pipelines (Methods). For the first pipeline, two human

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: with the linear marker (initial marker) every 3-10 slices, which is a com-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mon practice in tumor response evaluation. Then, MedSAM was used to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: segment the tumors based on these sparse linear annotations. Finally,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the expert manually revised the segmentation results until they were

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: satisfied. We quantitatively compared the annotation time cost between

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tance of MedSAM, the annotation time is substantially reduced by

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Discussion

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We introduce MedSAM, a deep learning-powered foundation model

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: designed for the segmentation of a wide array of anatomical structures

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and lesions across diverse medical imaging modalities. MedSAM is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: trained on a meticulously assembled large-scale dataset comprised of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: over one million medical image-mask pairs. Its promptable config-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: uration strikes an optimal balance between automation and customi-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: zation, rendering MedSAM a versatile tool for universal medical image

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: segmentation.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Through comprehensive evaluations encompassing both internal

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and external validation, MedSAM has demonstrated substantial cap-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: abilities in segmenting a diverse array of targets and robust general-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ization abilities to manage new data and tasks. Its performance not

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: only significantly exceeds that of existing the state-of-the-art seg-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mentation foundation model, but also rivals or even surpasses spe-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cialist models. By providing precise delineation of anatomical

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: structures and pathological regions, MedSAM facilitates the compu-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tation of various quantitative measures that serve as biomarkers. For

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Fig. 5 | The effect of training dataset size and a user study of tumor annotation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: efficiency. a Scaling up the training image size to one million can significantly

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: improve the model performance on both internal and external validation sets.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: instance, in the field of oncology, MedSAM could play a crucial role in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: accelerating the 3D tumor annotation process, enabling subsequent

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: calculations of tumor volume, which is a critical biomarker²9 for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: assessing disease progression and response to treatment. Additionally,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: MedSAM provides a successful paradigm for adapting natural image

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: foundation models to new domains, which can be further extended to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: biological image segmentation³0, such as cell segmentation in light

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: microscopy images³1 and organelle segmentation in electron micro-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: scopy images32.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: While MedSAM boasts strong capabilities, it does present certain

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: limitations. One such limitation is the modality imbalance in the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: training set, with CT, MRI, and endoscopy images dominating the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: dataset. This could potentially impact the model's performance on

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: less-represented modalities, such as mammography. Another limita-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion is its difficulty in the segmentation of vessel-like branching

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: structures because the bounding box prompt can be ambiguous in this

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: setting. For example, arteries and veins share the same bounding box

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in eye fundus images. However, these limitations do not diminish

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: MedSAM's utility. Since MedSAM has learned rich and representative

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: medical image features from the large-scale training set, it can be fine-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tuned to effectively segment new tasks from less-represented mod-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: alities or intricate structures like vessels.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In conclusion, this study highlights the feasibility of constructing a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: single foundation model capable of managing a multitude of seg-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mentation tasks, thereby eliminating the need for task-specific models.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: MedSAM, as the inaugural foundation model in medical image seg-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mentation, holds great potential to accelerate the advancement of new

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: diagnostic and therapeutic tools, and ultimately contribute to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: improved patient care33.

layout_dets.text: Methods

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Dataset curation and pre-processing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We curated a comprehensive dataset by collating images from publicly

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: available medical image segmentation datasets, which were obtained

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: from various sources across the internet, including the Cancer Imaging

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Archive (TCIA)³4, Kaggle, Grand-Challenge, Scientific Data, CodaLab,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and segmentation challenges in the Medical Image Computing and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Computer Assisted Intervention Society (MICCAI). All the datasets

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: provided segmentation annotations by human experts, which have

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: been widely used in existing literature (Supplementary Table 1-4). We

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: incorporated these annotations directly for both model development

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and validation.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The original 3D datasets consisted of computed tomography (CT)

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and magnetic resonance (MR) images in DICOM, nrrd, or mhd formats.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: To ensure uniformity and compatibility with developing medical

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: image deep learning models, we converted the images to the widely

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: used NifTI format. Additionally, grayscale images (such as X-Ray and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Ultrasound) as well as RGB images (including endoscopy, dermoscopy,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: fundus, and pathology images), were converted to the png format.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: b MedSAM can be used to substantially reduce the annotation time cost. Source

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: data are provided as a Source Data file.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Several exclusive criteria are applied to improve the dataset quality

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and consistency, including incomplete images and segmentation tar-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: gets with branching structures, inaccurate annotations, and tiny

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: volumes. Notably, image intensities varied significantly across differ-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ent modalities. For instance, CT images had intensity values ranging

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: from -2000 to 2000, while MR images exhibited a range of 0 to 3000.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In endoscopy and ultrasound images, intensity values typically span-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ned from 0 to 255. To facilitate stable training, we performed intensity

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: normalization across all images, ensuring they shared the same

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: intensity range.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: For CT images, we initially normalized the Hounsfield units using

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: typical window width and level values. The employed window width

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and level values for soft tissues, lung, and brain are (W:400, L:40),

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (W:1500, L:-160), and (W:80, L:40), respectively. Subsequently, the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: intensity values were rescaled to the range of [0, 255]. For MR, X-ray,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ultrasound, mammography, and optical coherence tomography (OCT)

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: images, we clipped the intensity values to the range between the 0.5th

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and 99.5th percentiles before rescaling them to the range of [0, 255].

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Regarding RGB images (e.g., endoscopy, dermoscopy, fundus, and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pathology images), if they were already within the expected intensity

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: range of [0, 255], their intensities remained unchanged. However, if

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: they fell outside this range, we utilized max-min normalization to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: rescale the intensity values to [0, 255]. Finally, to meet the model's

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: input requirements, all images were resized to a uniform size of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 1024 × 1024 × 3. In the case of whole-slide pathology images, patches

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: were extracted using a sliding window approach without overlaps. The

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: patches located on boundaries were padded to this size with 0. As for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3D CT and MR images, each 2D slice was resized to 1024 × 1024, and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the channel was repeated three times to maintain consistency. The

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: remaining 2D images were directly resized to 1024 × 1024 × 3. Bi-cubic

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: interpolation was used for resizing images, while nearest-neighbor

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: interpolation was applied for resizing masks to preserve their precise

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: boundaries and avoid introducing unwanted artifacts. These standar-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: dization procedures ensured uniformity and compatibility across all

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: images and facilitated seamless integration into the subsequent stages

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of the model training and evaluation pipeline.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Network architecture

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The network utilized in this study was built on transformer

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: architecture²7, which has demonstrated remarkable effectiveness in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: various domains such as natural language processing and image

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: recognition tasks2⁵5. Specifically, the network incorporated a vision

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: transformer (ViT)-based image encoder responsible for extracting

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: image features, a prompt encoder for integrating user interactions

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (bounding boxes), and a mask decoder that generated segmentation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: results and confidence scores using the image embedding, prompt

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: embedding, and output token.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: To strike a balance between segmentation performance and com-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: putational efficiency, we employed the base ViT model as the image

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: encoder since extensive evaluation indicated that larger ViT models,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: such as ViT Large and ViT Huge, offered only marginal improvements in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: accuracy while significantly increasing computational demands. Speci-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: fically, the base ViT model consists of 12 transformer layers²7, with each

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: block comprising a multi-head self-attention block and a Multilayer

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Perceptron (MLP) block incorporating layer normalization³5. Pre-training

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: was performed using masked auto-encoder modeling36, followed by

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: fully supervised training on the SAM dataset7. The input image

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (1024 × 1024 × 3) was reshaped into a sequence of flattened 2D patches

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: with the size 16 × 16 × 3, yielding a feature size in image embedding of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 64 × 64 after passing through the image encoder, which is 16 × down-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: scaled. The prompt encoders mapped the corner point of the bounding

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: box prompt to 256-dimensional vectorial embeddings26. In particular,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: each bounding box was represented by an embedding pair of the top-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: left corner point and the bottom-right corner point. To facilitate real-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: time user interactions once the image embedding had been computed, a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: lightweight mask decoder architecture was employed. It consists of two

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: transformer layers27 for fusing the image embedding and prompt

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: encoding, and two transposed convolutional layers to enhance the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: embedding resolution to 256 × 256. Subsequently, the embedding

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: underwent sigmoid activation, followed by bi-linear interpolations to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: match the input size.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Training protocol and experimental setting

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: During data pre-processing, we obtained 1,570,263 medical image-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mask pairs for model development and validation. For internal vali-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: dation, we randomly split the dataset into 80%, 10%, and 10% as

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: training, tuning, and validation, respectively. Specifically, for mod-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: alities where within-scan continuity exists, such as CT and MRI, and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: modalities where continuity exists between consecutive frames, we

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: performed the data splitting at the 3D scan and the video level

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: respectively, by which any potential data leak was prevented. For

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pathology images, recognizing the significance of slide-level cohe-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: siveness, we first separated the whole-slide images into distinct slide-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: based sets. Then, each slide was divided into small patches with a fixed

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: size of 1024 × 1024. This setup allowed us to monitor the model's

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: performance on the tuning set and adjust its parameters during

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: training to prevent overfitting. For the external validation, all datasets

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: were held out and did not appear during model training. These data-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sets provide a stringent test of the model's generalization ability, as

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: they represent new patients, imaging conditions, and potentially new

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: segmentation tasks that the model has not encountered before. By

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: evaluating the performance of MedSAM on these unseen datasets, we

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: can gain a realistic understanding of how MedSAM is likely to perform

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in real-world clinical settings, where it will need to handle a wide range

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of variability and unpredictability in the data. The training and vali-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: dation are independent.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The model was initialized with the pre-trained SAM model with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the ViT-Base model. We fixed the prompt encoder since it can already

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: encode the bounding box prompt. All the trainable parameters in the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: image encoder and mask decoder were updated during training.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.text: Human annotation study

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The objective of the human annotation study was to quantitatively

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: evaluate how MedSAM can reduce the annotation time cost. Specifi-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cally, we used the recent adrenocortical carcinoma CT dataset³4,42,43,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: where the segmentation target, adrenal tumor, was neither part of the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: training nor of the existing validation sets. We randomly sampled 10

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cases, comprising a total of 733 tumor slices requiring annotations.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Two human experts participated in this study, both of whom are

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: experienced radiologists with 8 and 6 years of clinical practice in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: abdominal diseases, respectively. Each expert generated two groups of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: annotations, one with the assistance of MedSAM and one without.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In the first group, the experts manually annotated the 3D adrenal

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tumor in a slice-by-slice manner. Annotations by the two experts were

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: conducted independently, with no collaborative discussions, and the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: time taken for each case was recorded. In the second group, annota-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tions were generated after one week of cooling period. The experts

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: independently drew the long and short tumor axes as initial markers,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: which is a common practice in tumor response evaluation. This pro-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cess was executed every 3-10 slices from the top slice to the bottom

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: slice of the tumor. Then, we applied MedSAM to segment the tumors

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: based on these sparse linear annotations, including three steps.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Step 1. For each annotated slice, a rectangle binary mask was

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: generated based on the linear label that can completely cover

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the linear label.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Step 2. For the unlabeled slices, the rectangle binary masks were

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: created through interpolation of the surrounding labeled slices.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Step 3. We transformed the binary masks into bounding boxes

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and then fed them along with the images into MedSAM to gen-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: erate segmentation results.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: All these steps were conducted in an automatic way and the model

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: running time was recorded for each case. Finally, human experts

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: manually refined the segmentation results until they met their satis-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: faction. To summarize, the time cost of the second group of annota-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tions contained three parts: initial markers, MedSAM inference, and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: refinement. All the manual annotation processes were based on ITK-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: SNAP⁴4, an open-source software designed for medical image visuali-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: zation and annotation.

layout_dets.text: Statistical analysis

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: To statistically analyze and compare the performance of the afore-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mentioned four methods (MedSAM, SAM, U-Net, and DeepLabV3+

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: specialist models), we employed the Wilcoxon signed-rank test. This

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: non-parametric test is well-suited for comparing paired samples and is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: normal distribution. This analysis allowed us to determine if any

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: method demonstrated statistically superior segmentation perfor-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mance compared to the others, providing valuable insights into the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: comparative effectiveness of the evaluated methods. The Wilcoxon
